text: The operation, the payload and the element names of the checked-fields read come from RWB-P5-E2025-CON and are never guessed; the treatment columns that carry the facts are named for the extracted codes (contract_amount, contract_date, mortgage_amount, registration_date, land_office, title_doc_no) with source_document_id, source_doc_version and source_table_version beside them, and the amounts and dates follow the numeric(18,2) and date conventions TSD S2 T3.1 already uses; the type-table version stamped on the row is the tableVersion of the reader's answer the facts were written from; and the masking of party_names is the hub's, applied to the value it returns, with this service storing no party name at all.
why: No source names the read across the boundary, no source gives the treatment a contract or mortgage column, no source says who stamps the type-table version, and the legacy note limits unmasked values to SY-CASEWF and SY-AGENT, which does not include this service; leaving any of them blank would make the story unbuildable, and inventing a business value would be worse.

text: This story is the secondary slice of legacy RWB-E2-025: the classification, the extraction, the review queue, the evaluation runner and the eleven legacy acceptance criteria AC1 to AC11 stay with RWB-P5-E2025-APP, and the two requirements of the plan's list that the legacy key puts out of scope (REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018) are answered by the document hub and tested by no criterion here. The story writes eight criteria of its own.

text: No personal data is written, logged or put on an event by this story: the row, the log lines, the workflow input and any event payload carry the case ID, the treatment ID, the document ID and version, the type-table version, field codes, amounts and dates only. party_names is masked by the hub, is never mapped onto a column, and a property test fails the build if a party name reaches a row, a log line or a span attribute.

text: This slice publishes no event and registers no Schedule, and both rows stay in the pattern list as prohibitions. DP-09 is used only through the outbox and inbox library for the idempotency table of rwb_treatment and the one write key of the apply: DocumentFieldsExtracted is produced by rwb-document and consumed by rwb-case only, and the two events of rwb-treatment, TreatmentApproved and TreatmentClosed, belong to the approval and plan stories. DP-10 registers nothing: the intake and retention Schedules are rwb-document's, and the stage clock the activity runs under is the parent workflow's.
why: Declaring a producer for an event that no source assigns would put an outbox row into a slice that owns no event, and declaring a Schedule would add a job no source places in this capability; carrying both as prohibitions keeps the pattern list intact and makes the reading visible.

Architecture v5 slide 16 publishes no inbound suggestion operation on rwb-agent, so the operation the primary slice publishes is read as an addition to the slide 16 list; the treatment service never embeds the agent, never calls the Enterprise AI endpoint and never reads an rwb_agent row.

confirm: Solution architect, owner of the architecture slide, and the rwb-agent contract owner

text: The stage waits at most 60 s for the answer and then uses the rule result of the RESTRUCTURE package version in force, with the fallback fact on the proposal and on the decision record, while the one REST hop also declares the 2 s client budget of DP-11. Either breach - the client budget or the 60 s wait - falls back and the stage continues on RESUME_STATE of R-UNI-32; no source reconciles the two waits, so both are declared and neither is dropped.
why: R-UNI-32 and Architecture v5 slide 16 fix 60 seconds, DP-11 fixes 2 s on a hop, and the same key carries both; the treatment side behaves the same under either.
read: R-UNI-32 (60 seconds, RESUME_STATE); Architecture v5 slide 16 ('AgentRunWorkflow: 60 s, then rule result'); Temporal and Drools Design slide 27; DP-11; ASM-B-P10-03-E2032-3
confirm: Solution architect and the platform architecture review
impact: A slow agent never stops a case and the officer always sees a proposal; the treatment side records which of the two produced it.

text: No personal data leaves the service on the agent call. The request carries the case ID, the treatment ID, the route, the band and the plan terms as identifiers and amounts; a name, an account number, a national identifier, an address or a document text is never sent, stored on the proposal, written to the decision record, put on the outbox event or logged. The masked inputs snapshot of the legacy is assembled by P10 rwb-agent behind its own contract, not here.
why: CTL-11 and the architecture note on agent risk require prompts, outputs and model versions to be logged while personal data stays out of logs, events and workflow inputs; the legacy masks the inputs on the agent side.
read: Legacy section 17; CTL-11; Architecture v5 slides 42, 43 and 44 (events carry IDs and facts, never personal data; human decision on material actions); NFR-052 and NFR-054
confirm: Risk and model risk, and the data protection review
impact: The property test of AC7 stands over the request, the answer, the record, the event payload and the logs; the boundary needs no extra control.

text: The decision-record writer RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, the parameters client RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, the reference-data client RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, the composite route RWB-PLT-N001-CON, the access guard and the embedded Drools runtime are the wave 0 service-template capability, so this story declares the patterns and the dependency each adds and carries no H build dependency, which is why the Work Package lists Depends on (build) as None and one contract dependency only.

read: Architecture v5 slides 20 and 41; DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-19; ASM-B-S2-01-02 and ASM-B-S2-01-03; the Work Package B-S2-06 story line
